legend: Angiography demonstrating distinctive serpentine increase in vascularity in hibernoma.
By MRI, soft tissue hibernoma is isointense to subcutaneous fat on both T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and gadolinium-enhanced imaging.
Gross pathology portends the hibernoma as yellow-brown, with delicate fibrous septa and lobular appearance.
Multivacuolated brown fat cells with centrally located small nucleus.
S100 positive (cytoplasmic and nuclear). Intraosseous hibernoma cells are always negative for brachyury and cytokeratins.

legend: Axial T1-weighted (shown here) and short-tau inversion recovery (STIR) (Fig. <<56709>>) imaging of a hibernoma in the left supraclavicular fossa. This demonstrates high T1 signal, with suppression on STIR imaging, in keeping with a fat-containing lesion. Incomplete suppression and signal heterogeneity are in keeping with a degree of atypia.
source: Dr Huw Walters and Dr Rajat Chowdhury, Department of Radiology, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford, UK
